title: Indian Railways Approves Rs 1,236 Crore Projects To Expand Kavach Safety System And Strengthen Fibre Communication Network
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Mar 26, 2026 | Updated 10:09 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

Indian Railways has cleared infrastructure projects worth about Rs 1,236 crore to strengthen its communication backbone and expand the deployment of the Kavach automatic train protection system across key routes.
The approvals cover three separate proposals focused on optical fibre infrastructure in the Central and Western Railway zones and the rollout of Kavach on busy sections of Southern Railway.
A major portion of the investment will go towards upgrading the communication network on Central Railway. Projects valued at Rs 623.63 crore will establish a dual-path fibre communication system across the zone’s five divisions — Solapur, Nagpur, Pune, Bhusawal and Mumbai.
The first component involves installing Optical Ground Wire (OPGW) with 96 fibre capacity along 2,250.68 route km of existing 25 KV traction lines across the Solapur, Nagpur, Pune and Bhusawal divisions.
The composite overhead wire will function both as a protection wire for the traction system and as a medium for high-capacity optical fibre communication, eliminating the need for additional civil infrastructure.
In parallel, underground optical fibre cables with 2x48 fibre capacity will be laid along 2,673.21 route km across all five divisions.
Together, the overhead and underground fibre lines will create two independent communication paths along each route, ensuring network reliability even if one line fails.
The additional fibre capacity will also be available for leasing as dark fibre, offering a potential revenue stream for the railways.
Meanwhile, Southern Railway will see the expansion of the Kavach safety system over 548 route km for Rs 310.18 crore.
The system will be deployed on sections including Jolarpettai–Erode, Chennai Beach–Tambaram–Chengalpattu and Shoranur–Mangalore, covering key routes across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.
Western Railway will also undertake fibre network expansion worth Rs 302.25 crore to complete the communication infrastructure across the Rajkot and Bhavnagar divisions in Gujarat.
